newsitem.title: USA: Ascent Entertainment seeks credit extension.
newsitem.headline: Ascent Entertainment seeks credit extension.

text.p: Ascent Entertainment Group Inc said Monday it is negotiating an extension of a bank credit facility that could fall into default unless the company commenced construction of a new Denver arena by Aug. 31.
Ascent, which was spun off last month from Comsat Corp, said it will not be able to break ground on the new arena by the Aug. 31 deadline.
Ascent also said it may only renew the credit line for an additional two years beyond Oct. 9 if it has received $50 million in subordinated debt financing.
The company said it is also continuing negotiations with both the city and county of Denver over the arena project in addition to negotiating with its lenders.

Ascent said it believes its credit extension discussions "will be successful," but added "there can be no assurances that other contingencies will not arise which could impact Ascent's ability to reach final agreements with its lenders and obtain the additional subordinated financing or that such financing will be available on terms acceptable to Ascent."
Ascent also said that as a result of its recent spinoff from Comsat, its financial leverage may increase, "subject to the resolution of the bank financing issues."

The company said that in order to protect the tax-free status of the spinoff it will not be able to issue stock or sell instruments convertible into stock until a year after the date of the spinoff. The spinoff was completed June 27.

The company said it will not realize revenues from its Beacon Communications unit's summer film release "Air Force One" until the third quarter. The feature film, which opened July 25, earned $37.1 million over its first weekend at the box office.
